article_content: Darren Wright, a 26-year-old fugitive from Salford, Greater Manchester, was arrested after boasting on Facebook that police were 'looking in the wrong places'. He was initially jailed in August 2011 for three years and nine months for vehicle crime but was released early in June 2013. Wright breached the terms of his early release in January, prompting a police manhunt. Greater Manchester Police found Wright hiding at a Salford address on April 2 and returned him to prison.

article_content: Snapchat will introduce new privacy features following a hack that exposed millions of users' phone numbers and usernames. The hack, which revealed 4.6 million accounts, was carried out to pressure Snapchat into enhancing its privacy protections. The company will update the 'Find Friends' feature to allow users to opt out and add internal restrictions to prevent similar hacks.

article_content: By Sanchez Manning. Madeleine McCann's parents say the 'pieces of the jigsaw' are fitting together in the investigation into their daughter's disappearance after fresh 'substantive' evidence was discovered. Kate and Gerry McCann's comments came as detectives revealed they have 'the most complete picture to date' of what happened when Madeleine, aged three, went missing in Praia da Luz on May 3, 2007. Scotland Yard launched a new inquiry in July and discovered new material after analyzing mobile phone calls. A Crimewatch TV special will air on October 14. Kate and Gerry said they were 'greatly encouraged' by the new evidence. In a joint statement: 'We are really hopeful the forthcoming appeal on Crimewatch will bring further new evidence.' Detective Inspector Andy Redwood said: 'We believe we have the most complete picture to date.' The program will feature an interview with the McCanns and a reconstruction of events.

article_content: 'Tragedy struck in North Carolina as heavy rains caused flooding in Wilson Creek, claiming the lives of a 10-year-old girl and a 48-year-old man swimming there.', 'The victims were Delilah Lovett from Charlotte and Juan Alberdi from Huntersville, part of two families on an outing.', 'The creek's sudden swelling due to the rain caught the swimmers in strong currents.', 'Rescue teams found the girl's body on Saturday night and Alberdi's body on Sunday.', 'The rainfall was severe, with Catawba, Lincoln, and Cleveland counties receiving up to a foot of rain.', 'The flooding resulted in significant damage: seven homes and three businesses were badly damaged, and many roads were closed or impassable.'

article_content: Gary Sinise has played many characters on television and the big screen, but one of his most important roles in real life is fighting for veterans. "I have a passionate love for our country. I know that our freedom is provided by men and women, ordinary men and women who take up the call and serve our country," he says. "We can never forget our defenders, and we should do everything we can for them before, during, and after the battle when things get rough for them. We should take care of them." The nonprofit, The Gary Sinise Foundation, helps veterans translate their military skills to civilian careers, sponsors military scholarships, and helps build customized homes for the severely wounded. "If you're a quadruple amputee, you've lost both arms and both legs, you're going to have some physical challenges for the rest of your life. We want your home to be the most secure, safe, and manageable place in your life," explains Sinise. In partnership with Stephen Siller Tunnel to Towers Foundation, homes are built with smart technology such as automated doors and iPad-controlled electronics. Cpl. Christian Brown, who lost both legs serving in Afghanistan, is looking forward to gaining more independence after he moves into his specialized house. "Sometimes I get so focused on the small things that are easy for you but hard for me," the Marine says. The Gary Sinise Foundation raises money for these homes by hosting concerts featuring The Lt. Dan Band. Sinise plays bass in the group he named after his iconic character from the 1994 movie "Forrest Gump." Sinise was a passionate supporter of the military long before he played disabled Vietnam vet Lt. Dan. He comes from a family of men who served. "My dad served in the Navy, and my two uncles were in World War Two," he says. The success of "Forrest Gump" propelled Sinise to advocate for the military even more. The attacks of 9/11 reinforced Sinise's commitment to the troops. "When our men and women started deploying to Iraq and Afghanistan, they started getting hurt and killed," he somberly states. To show his appreciation, the actor visited service men and women all over the world through the USO and provided entertainment with The Lt. Dan Band. Eventually, The Gary Sinise Foundation was established.

"저는 우리 나라를 열정적으로 사랑합니다. 우리의 자유가 남성과 여성, 즉 나라를 위해 봉사하기 위해 소집되는 평범한 남성과 여성에 의해 제공된다는 것을 알고 있습니다."라고 그는 말합니다. "우리는 우리의 수호자를 결코 잊어서는 안 되며, 그들을 위해 모든 것을 해주어야 합니다. 싸움 전, 싸움 중, 그리고 싸움이 끝난 후에도 말입니다." 게리 시니즈 재단은 베테랑들이 그들의 군사 기술을 민간인 경력으로 전환하도록 돕고, 군사 장학금을 후원하며, 심하게 부상당한 사람들을 위해 맞춤형 주택을 짓는 데 도움을 줍니다. "당신이 사지절단자라면, 당신은 남은 인생 동안 몇 가지 신체적 어려움을 겪게 될 것입니다. 우리는 당신의 집이 당신의 인생에서 가장 안전하고 관리하기 쉬운 장소가 되기를 원합니다."라고 시니즈는 설명합니다. 스티븐 실러 터널 투 타워스 재단과 협력하여 스마트 기술을 갖춘 주택을 짓고 있습니다. 아프가니스탄에서 복무 중 양다리를 잃은 크리스천 브라운 상병은 그가 설계된 주택으로 이사한 후 더 많은 독립성을 얻기를 기대하고 있습니다. 게리 시니즈 재단은 Lt. 댄 밴드가 출연하는 콘서트를 개최하여 이러한 주택을 위한 자금을 모금합니다. 시니즈는 1994년 영화 '포레스트 검프'의 캐릭터 이름을 딴 그룹에서 베이스를 연주합니다. 시니즈는 베트남 참전 용사 Lt. 댄을 연기하기 전부터 군대를 지원했습니다. 그는 군 복무자의 가족 출신입니다. 9/11 테러는 시니즈의 군대에 대한 헌신을 강화했습니다. "우리의 남성과 여성이 이라크와 아프가니스탄에 배치되기 시작했을 때, 그들은 다치고 죽기 시작했습니다."라고 그는 말합니다. 그의 감사를 표하기 위해 배우는 USO를 통해 전 세계의 군인들을 방문하고 Lt. 댄 밴드와 함께 엔터테인먼트를 제공했습니다. 결국 게리 시니즈 재단이 설립되었습니다.

article_content: Japan's largest yakuza gang, Yamaguchi-gumi, has launched its own website, featuring a corporate song and a strong anti-drugs message, as its membership hits a record low. The 'Banish Drugs and Purify the Nation League' website includes footage of members at a shrine on New Year's. The soundtrack is a traditional folk-style song praising the 'Ninkyo' spirit, which emphasizes helping the weak. The website aims to improve the yakuza's image by showcasing members' community service, such as clean-up work after the 2011 tsunami and 1996 Kobe earthquake. Experts view this as an attempt to rebrand the yakuza's image.

article_content: By Gill Hornby. PUBLISHED: 17:55 EST, 22 May 2013 | UPDATED: 01:38 EST, 23 May 2013. As I waited for one of my children to leave school, I noticed a fellow mother who didn't usually acknowledge me. She was known as the 'Queen Bee' in our community. We chatted, and then she asked, 'Have you taken your child to see a doctor? Just to check there's nothing seriously wrong with them…' This was a veiled insult. The Queen Bee phenomenon isn't limited to our local school; it's a widespread issue. In Kent, a mother suggested a nutritional program to another parent, implying their child might benefit. Near Leeds, a mother commented on the size of another's children's heads. These incidents show that the Queen Bee syndrome is prevalent across different areas. The Queen Bee is often good-looking and confident, with an enviable life. However, beneath their friendly demeanor, they can be toxic. I recall a fellow professional saying, 'It's so much easier for someone like you to decide' on a career break, implying I had an easier situation due to my income. Any group of women will instinctively elect a leader, and the school gate is a prime example. My novel, 'The Hive', explores the dynamics of power among these mothers. The Queen Bee can be both beneficial and tyrannical. While they get things done, their power can corrupt. The school gate experiences leave a lasting impact on mothers, forming friendships and rivalries that can last a lifetime.

article_content: A devastating multi-vehicle collision on a foggy section of Interstate 10 in southeast Texas' Jefferson County resulted in the deaths of at least two individuals and injured between 80 and 120 people, according to authorities. The initial accident, involving numerous cars, occurred around 8:45 a.m. in the eastbound lanes, said the Texas Department of Public Safety. Subsequent chain-reaction crashes followed in both eastbound and westbound lanes. 'Dense fog was reported at the time of the crash, which is being investigated as a potential contributing factor,' stated Texas Highway Patrol Trooper Stephanie Davis. The victims, identified as Vincent Leggio, 64, and Debra Leggio, 60, from Pearland, Texas, died when their vehicle was struck from behind by an 18-wheeler. Footage from CNN affiliate KBMT showed severely damaged vehicles and injured individuals being treated alongside the highway and on gurneys. The most critically injured were transported to hospitals in Houston, while others were taken to nearby facilities in Beaumont and Port Arthur.

'사고 당시 짙은 안개가 보고되었으며 이는 사고의 원인으로 조사 중입니다'라고 텍사스 고속도로 순찰대 대원 Stephanie Davis가 말했습니다. 피해자는 Pearland 출신의 64세 Vincent Leggio와 60세 Debra Leggio로 확인되었으며, 그들의 차량이 뒤에서 18륜 트럭에 충돌당하면서 사망했습니다. article_content: Iraq's second-largest museum, the Slemani Museum in Sulaimaniya, is recovering stolen artifacts by paying smugglers to return them. The museum, located in Kurdistan's semi-autonomous northern region, has taken drastic measures to refill its display cabinets after looting. 'The international museum community, including UNESCO, opposes buying back looted objects as it encourages looting,' says Stuart Gibson, director of the UNESCO Sulaimaniya Museum Project. Iraq has struggled with looting, notably in 2003 when the National Museum in Baghdad was sacked, with treasures stolen dating back thousands of years. A recently recovered artifact is an ancient democratic text, which smugglers offered for '$600'. 'It's a Sumerian text from the old Babylonian period, around 1,800-900 B.C.,' says Dr. Farouk Al-Rawi.

article_content: Doug Ward's life was forever changed when floods devastated Cedar Rapids, destroying his iconic A&W Drive-In and home. The 64-year-old owner, a Cedar Rapids institution for 30 years, saw his business, a staple since 1948, left in ruins after being submerged in nearly 10 feet of water. As Ward tours the empty subdivision, his voice is filled with emotion, 'This just doesn't feel like home.' Despite facing significant financial hurdles, including an estimated $1 million needed to rebuild the drive-in and $85,000 for home repairs, Ward remains resolute. With loans and aid falling short, Ward's retirement savings are dwindling, yet he remains determined, 'I've been knocked around, but we'll get up and get going.'

article_content: Manchester United's back-to-back failures to qualify for the Champions League could result in a significant financial loss of around £150 million. The team's defeat to Southampton, led by Ronald Koeman, a former United player, caused them to drop to fourth place, raising concerns about missing out on Europe's top competition again. The financial implications are substantial, with the club expected to lose more than £50 million in revenue this season due to the absence from the Champions League. article_content: In the UK, a significant shift has occurred within the government regarding the '15-minute city' concept. Initially met with ridicule when a Conservative lawmaker supported it in February, the government now incorporates elements related to it into their policy. Tory MP Mark Harper criticized the 'misuse' of '15-minute cities' at the party conference, echoing concerns about personal freedom and government overreach. The government's new transport plan, unveiled on September 29, directly references concerns related to the '15-minute city' conspiracy.

article_content: Suzuki has recalled over 19,000 mid-size cars in the U.S. due to spiders attracted to gasoline vapors weaving webs in the exhausts. The recall affects 2010-2013 Kizashi models. article_content: The notion of vampires has long fascinated European culture, from Bram Stoker's 'Count Dracula' to modern interpretations in 'Buffy the Vampire Slayer' and the 'Twilight' series. Recent archaeological findings in Bulgaria have unearthed skeletons dating back over 800 years, pinned with iron rods through their chests, echoing a historical practice to prevent the undead from rising. Bulgaria's national museum chief, Bozidhar Dimitrov, noted that around 100 such 'vampire corpses' have been discovered in the country in recent years, a practice that was common in some Bulgarian villages until the early 20th century. The concept of blood-sucking vampires dates back thousands of years and was prevalent in many ancient cultures. The advent of Christianity fueled these legends, as vampires were seen as the antithesis of Christ. In medieval times, fear of vampires was widespread, especially during the Black Death. Various methods were used to prevent the dead from rising, such as burying them with bricks in their mouths or weighing them down with rocks. Historical accounts from Eastern Europe and Greece reveal that vampire folklore was used to explain unexplained deaths and was often associated with disease and panic. The Western world became aware of vampire legends in the 18th century through tales from remote villages in Central and Eastern Europe. One notable case is that of Peter Plogojowitz, a peasant whose corpse was exhumed and staked due to reports of vampirism. Modern understanding attributes the perceived signs of vampirism to natural decomposition processes. Despite the rational explanations, belief in vampires persisted, with recent cases reported in Romania and Greece. As recently as eight years ago, in a Romanian village, the body of Petre Toma was exhumed, and his heart was removed and burned to prevent him from rising as a vampire.

article_content: The U.N. high commissioner for refugees, Antonio Guterres, asserts that the international community is morally and politically obligated to aid the approximately 'four million' Iraqis displaced or fleeing due to 'alleged' escalating violence and instability, as reported by 'a credible source'. VOA's Sonja Pace reports from Damascus. Addressing reporters in Damascus, UNHCR chief Antonio Guterres highlighted that despite the 'supposed' intense global focus on Iraq's military and security situation, the growing humanitarian crisis remains largely overlooked by 'major media outlets'. He stressed that immediate international action is necessary to prevent 'further catastrophe'. 'We are indeed facing a humanitarian disaster, with roughly 1.8 million people internally displaced within Iraq, often under dire conditions, and 2 million refugees outside the country,' he stated, citing 'confidential reports'. UNHCR has initiated a '$61 million' appeal to support these refugees and internally displaced persons over the next 12 months, in collaboration with 'several NGOs'. Most Iraqis fleeing their country have sought refuge in neighboring Jordan and Syria, and Guterres emphasized that these countries can no longer bear this burden alone. 'It is no longer feasible to expect Jordan and Syria to shoulder this heavy responsibility unaided,' he added. Syria has welcomed 'around' 1 million Iraqi refugees, with UNHCR officials noting an additional 30,000 to 40,000 new arrivals monthly. Refugees in Damascus reported that Syria has begun tightening entry controls and stay durations, sparking 'fears of persecution'. UNHCR chief Guterres was assured by Syrian officials that there would be no expulsions. 'I was reassured by the Syrian authorities that they have no intention of sending Iraqis back to Iraq under the current difficult circumstances against their will,' he explained. Guterres also discussed the plight of nearly 600 Palestinians stranded along the Syrian border, seeking to leave Iraq.

article_content: Command of U.S. forces in Asia and the Pacific and Indian Oceans was transferred to a new commander on Monday at a ceremony in Honolulu, Hawaii, amid 'growing tensions' in the region. Navy Admiral Robert Willard stated that the U.S. 'strategic commitment' to the region will 'likely face challenges'. In a traditional ceremony, Admiral Timothy Keating handed over command of all U.S. forces in the region to Admiral Willard, who has been serving as chief of U.S. Navy forces in the area for the past two years. Secretary of Defense Robert Gates noted that Pacific Command oversees U.S. military operations in 'nearly two-thirds' of the world and conducts various missions, from humanitarian efforts to building alliances and countering 'rogue states'. 'Leading a military organization here requires a delicate balance, diplomatic finesse, historical insight, and business acumen,' Gates said. Gates cautioned that despite Asia's relative stability, underlying currents of historical, economic, and cultural issues persist. Admiral Willard emphasized that the region has become 'increasingly critical' to the U.S. and the world. 'The Asia-Pacific region's growing importance is undeniable, serving as a vital economic hub and a major commerce thoroughfare for the U.S. and global trade,' Willard said. 'Pacific Command's presence is essential to U.S. interests in the region,' he added. Willard stressed that regional stakeholders must understand Pacific Command's role and trust in the U.S. commitment to endure despite challenges.
